Close-up of the sister array left by Apollo 14 in February 1971. Like Apollo 11's, it holds 100 corner cubes.
Artist's concept of a Mars Exploration Rover. Spirit and Opportunity were identical twins.
The bright soil Spirit's dragging wheel uncovered in 2007, nicknamed Gertrude Weise. It is about 90% silica. The track is about 20 cm wide.
Spirit's view from Troy, where it became embedded in soft soil in spring 2009.
InSight's final selfie, 24 April 2022 (sol 1,211). Compare the dust with its first selfie in 2018.
The wind and thermal shield covering InSight's seismometer on Mars, sol 110 (April 2019).
InSight's deck on sol 8 (December 2018): the seismometer (copper cover), its gray shield and the black heat probe, before the arm moved them to the ground.
Descent stage only. We made this version by deleting the ascent stage from NASA's model; nothing was added or reshaped.
NASA's complete Apollo Lunar Module model, both stages.
NASA's simplified model of Opportunity (MER-B). Spirit and Opportunity were identical twins.
NASA's InSight lander model (arm deployed). It shows SEIS and the heat probe on the deck, where they traveled to Mars.
